name: ArchWeave
description: A self-hosted architecture workspace that a developer (in the browser) and a coding agent (over MCP) edit together. One Node process serves the web UI, a REST + SSE API and a stateless MCP endpoint over one shared in-memory model, which is persisted as Git-friendly JSON in the modeled repository's `.archweave/` directory.

elements.name: AgentPresence
elements.summary: Whether an agent has called MCP recently, and its client name.

fields.name: connected
fields.description: True for 60 s after the last MCP request

elements.name: API error
elements.summary: Error body of REST failures: a readable message and, for invalid change sets, the validation details.
elements.description: 400 for ChangeError/PathError/ExportError/bad requests, 403 from the host guard, 409 for nothing to undo or a change set built from an older revision (`RevisionConflict`), 415 for a non-JSON body. The browser turns `error` into an error toast.

elements.name: App chrome
elements.summary: Top bar, command palette, export dialog, agent presence and activity feed, toasts, empty state and shortcuts.
elements.description: The empty state suggests the first agent prompt and shows the MCP connection snippet. The export dialog downloads Markdown/Mermaid/JSON from the server or captures the active canvas as PNG/SVG in the browser (html-to-image).

elements.name: apply_changes input
elements.summary: A ChangeSet with a required summary and an optional dryRun flag.
elements.description: Result: ChangeResult (with `dryRun: true` when validating only), plus `humanChangesSinceYouLastLooked` when the human changed the model since the agent last looked. A stale `expectedRevision` is a tool error.

fields.name: layout
fields.description: Accepted by the schema but agents are told not to send it

elements.name: ArchWeave server
elements.summary: One Node process that owns the model and serves the UI, REST/SSE API and MCP endpoint on one port.
elements.description:
Started by `src/server/main.ts` (dev: `tsx watch`; prod: esbuild bundle `dist/server/main.js`). Ships as a Docker image (`ghcr.io/rawe/archweave`) run next to the modeled repository with Docker Compose, which mounts the repo at `/repo`. Listens on `127.0.0.1:4317` by default.

All mutations — from the browser and from the agent — go through one `Store.apply(changeSet, actor)`.
elements.technology: Node 22, Hono 4, MCP TypeScript SDK, Zod 4

codeRefs.note: Wires store, persistence, session, routes and MCP
How a repository runs ArchWeave next to its code

elements.name: Canonical JSON
elements.summary: Writes the model in a stable on-disk form so Git diffs stay small and semantic.
elements.description: Arrays sorted by id, keys in schema order, default-valued fields omitted, layout coordinates rounded to 0.1. `explicitModel` is the opposite (all defaults filled in) and is used by the JSON export.

elements.name: Change engine
elements.summary: Applies a change set to a draft copy of the model with upsert semantics, list helpers and referential checks.

elements.name: ChangeResult
elements.summary: What applying a change set did: new revision, ids created/updated/removed and warnings.

fields.name: warnings
fields.description: e.g. references cleaned up after a removal

elements.name: ChangeSet
elements.summary: The one mutation shape: the browser posts it over REST, the agent sends it through apply_changes.
elements.description: Applied atomically by the store: all entries validate or nothing changes. `remove` cascades to descendants, attached relations and flow steps. A change set with only `layout` is not journaled.

fields.name: expectedRevision
fields.description: Revision the change set was built from; at another revision nothing is applied (409 over REST, a tool error over MCP). Ignored by layout-only change sets

elements.name: check_code_links result
elements.summary: Stale code refs with their owner's name and built elements without code refs; with `repair: true`, also what was re-anchored.
elements.description: Actors, externals and systems are exempt from `builtWithoutCode`. With `repair: true`, `stale` lists what still needs attention after the repair.

fields.name: hint
fields.description: Read-only call: how many refs moved, i.e. what repair would handle

fields.name: summary
fields.description: repair only: the journal summary, when anything changed

fields.name: repaired
fields.type: {ownerType, ownerId, ownerName, step?, path, symbol?, from: {startLine, endLine}, to: {startLine, endLine}}[]
fields.description: repair only: the moved refs that were re-anchored

elements.name: Client state
elements.summary: The browser's copy of the model plus view state, with optimistic edits reconciled against server snapshots.
elements.description: The displayed model is always *server snapshot + pending change sets applied locally*. `commit` applies a change set immediately, posts it, and marks it acknowledged with the returned revision; `receiveSnapshot` drops pending entries the server has caught up with. Agent journal entries mark touched ids as fresh/unseen and raise a toast with a *Show* action. Also holds perspective, scope, flow, selection, overlays and toasts.

elements.name: Code drawer
elements.summary: Shows a linked file with the referenced lines highlighted, plus an open-in-editor link.

elements.name: Code file
elements.summary: GET /api/code/file response: one repository file's content and facts for the code drawer.

elements.name: Code link checker
elements.summary: Checks code refs against the repository; for sealed refs it compares the linked text, so it tells moved code from edited code.
elements.description:
A ref with a line range is **sealed** when it is written: `seal` stores a `digest` of the linked lines (SHA-256 over the trimmed lines, first 12 base64url characters) in the ref.

`verdict` checks a sealed ref by its text: digest still matches → only the plain checks; the same text found verbatim elsewhere in the file (nearest first, with its symbol inside) → `moved` with a `suggestion`; otherwise → `changed`, with a suggestion where the symbol is now when that is unambiguous. Unsealed refs get only the plain checks: missing-file, line-out-of-range, symbol-not-found, symbol-outside-range.

File facts are cached by mtime and size. A symbol matches as a whole identifier outside quotes; for qualified names (`Store.apply`) the last segment is enough. Binary files (a NUL byte in the first 8000 bytes) and files over 1 MB are checked for existence only and never sealed. `access` gives the store what it needs to write refs: `seal` (synchronous, because the store applies change sets synchronously) and `normalizePath`. Used by `GET /api/code/stale`, `get_context` (count), `find_by_code` (check per ref), `check_code_links` and the change engine (sealing, verifying sent digests, normalizing paths).

codeRefs.note: Per-ref check: text of sealed refs first, then lines and symbol
Finds where sealed text moved to

elements.name: Code link repair
elements.summary: Re-anchors moved code refs in one journaled, revision-checked change set.
elements.description:
`repairCodeLinks` inspects the refs in scope (with `scopeId`: the subtree, plus relations and flow steps touching it) and applies one change set through the store with `expectedRevision` set: moved refs get their suggested range and keep their digest, so the store verifies the text at each new range. `changed` and other stale refs are never touched and come back in `stale`. There is no separate sealing step: a ref is sealed whenever it is written.

When the model or a file changed between check and apply (a `RevisionConflict`, or a digest that no longer matches), it checks once more (2 attempts); what it still cannot apply is reported in `stale`, not written. Agents reach it through `check_code_links` with `repair: true` (actor agent), the browser through `POST /api/code/repair` (actor human).

codeRefs.note: One patch per owner: moved refs relocated with their digests

elements.name: CodeRef
elements.summary: A link from the model into the repository: path, optional symbol and line range, sealed by the server.
elements.description:
Paths are stored normalized: repo-relative, forward slashes, no `./`; an absolute path inside the repository is made relative, one outside it is rejected. A ref may point at a directory.

A ref with a line range carries a `digest`, the seal of the linked lines, computed by the server whenever the ref is written. It lets the checker tell moved code from edited code. A ref written with a digest claims it is still the same code: kept when unchanged, verified against the file when its location changed, rejected when the text there differs. Clients send a ref without digest to seal it to the current text and never invent one.

Link a large unit by its declaration line (`symbol` + `startLine`, no `endLine`): the one-line seal follows the unit when it moves and survives edits to its body. A range is for a short passage whose exact lines are the point.

fields.name: symbol
fields.description: Function, class, type or export name; checked as an identifier

fields.name: digest
fields.description: Seal of the linked lines (12 base64url chars of SHA-256 over trimmed lines), set by the server. A sent digest must match the text at the ref's range, or the change set is rejected

elements.name: Coding agent
elements.summary: Reads the repository and keeps the model in sync with the code through MCP tools.
elements.description: Any MCP client (Claude Code, etc.) connected to `/mcp` over Streamable HTTP. It receives the modeling guide as the server's MCP instructions, analyzes code, applies change sets, reads the human's selection and repairs stale code links.

codeRefs.note: Modeling guide every agent receives as MCP instructions

elements.name: Model data directory
elements.summary: Holds the model, layout and activity journal as JSON files inside the modeled repository.
elements.description: Default `<repo>/.archweave` (`ARCHWEAVE_DATA_DIR`). `model.json` and `layout.json` are meant to be committed; `state/` (journal) is git-ignored by a `.gitignore` the server writes on first start. The server watches the directory and reloads files changed by someone else (git checkout, manual edit).

elements.name: Data perspective
elements.summary: Catalog of all data structures grouped by owner, and a focus view of one structure with what it references and who uses it.

codeRefs.note: Deterministic focus layout: referenced right, referencing left, users around

elements.name: Developer
elements.summary: Explores and edits the architecture in the browser and directs the coding agent.
elements.description: Selects elements, pins notes, edits names/fields/relations, arranges the layout and exports documentation. Their selection and open notes are what the agent reads through `get_context`.

elements.name: Element
elements.summary: A node of the architecture graph: system, actor, app, service, component, module, store, queue, agent or data structure.
elements.description: Containment is `parentId`. The data-only fields (`format`, `fields`, `example`) are meaningful for kind `data`. Ids are readable slugs, stable across renames.

fields.name: summary
fields.description: One sentence, shown on the diagram

fields.name: parentId
fields.description: Containing element; absent at the top level

elements.name: ElementPatch
elements.summary: An element upsert: every Element field optional, plus additive list helpers.
elements.description: With an existing id only the given fields change; with a new id (or none) `kind` and `name` are required. Within one patch the full list is applied first, then removals, then additions. Defaults are unwrapped (`patchShape`) so a patch never overwrites unspecified fields with defaults. RelationPatch is the same idea for relations (with `addCodeRefs`/`removeCodeRefs`).

fields.name: parentId
fields.description: null moves to the top level

fields.name: setFields
fields.description: Upsert by name; ref: null clears

elements.name: Export request
elements.summary: What to export: format, optional scope, perspectives and whether to include code refs.
elements.description: REST: `GET /api/export?format=markdown|mermaid|json&scope=&perspectives=structure,data,flows&code=true|false` returns a download with a filename. MCP `export` takes only `format` and `scope` and returns the text.

elements.name: Exporter
elements.summary: Renders the model as a Markdown architecture document, Mermaid diagrams only, or explicit JSON.
elements.description: Markdown: overview, one Mermaid flowchart per scope (using the same structure projection as the canvas) with element entries, data structures with field tables and an ER-style diagram, flows as sequence diagrams. Can be limited to a scope subtree and to some perspectives, with or without code refs.

elements.name: Field
elements.summary: One field of a data structure; may reference another data structure.

fields.name: type
fields.description: Free text, default ""; enum values go here

fields.name: ref
fields.description: Must name an element of kind data

elements.name: find_by_code result
elements.summary: Elements, relations and flow steps whose code refs touch given paths, with the current check of every ref, and the paths nothing links to.
elements.description: Every returned ref carries `check` ("ok" or a stale reason, including moved and changed) and, when known, `suggestion`. `hint` says what to do next: repair moved refs with `check_code_links`, fix the others with `apply_changes`.

fields.name: flowSteps
fields.type: {flowId, flowName, step, from, to, label, codeRefs: (CodeRef & {check, suggestion?})[]}[]

elements.name: Flow
elements.summary: A named scenario: an ordered walk through the architecture.

elements.name: FlowPatch
elements.summary: A flow upsert with index-based step helpers.
elements.description: Indices are 0-based and refer to the step list before this patch (after `steps`, if sent).

elements.name: FlowStep
elements.summary: One ordered step of a flow: who talks to whom, with what data.

elements.name: Flows perspective
elements.summary: Lists flows and draws the selected one as a sequence diagram whose steps can be stepped through and edited.

elements.name: FocusRequest
elements.summary: Sent by the agent to steer the human's view to some elements with a message.

elements.name: focus_ui input
elements.summary: Elements to highlight and where to navigate; validated, then published to browsers as a FocusRequest.

elements.name: get_context result
elements.summary: What the human sees and has selected, expanded in full, plus open notes, their recent changes and the stale-link count.

fields.name: humanChanges
fields.description: Human entries since the agent's cursor

fields.name: ui.dataView
fields.type: {state: 'catalog', structures, groups: {owner, count}[]} | {state: 'focus', structure, references, referencedBy, users: {verb, elements}[]}
fields.description: Data perspective: the catalog, or the first selected data structure in focus, as the browser draws it

elements.name: get_model input
elements.summary: Which part of the outline to return: scope, depth, kinds and whether to include data structures.

elements.name: Health check
elements.summary: Tells Docker and people whether the server is up and its model is loaded.
elements.description:
`GET /api/health` returns `{ status: 'ok', version, revision }`: the server version (same as the MCP server reports) and the current model revision. The version is `ARCHWEAVE_VERSION` when set (the Docker image sets it from its `VERSION` build arg), else the version in package.json, inlined into the bundle.

It is an `/api` route, registered before the static UI handler, so it answers whether or not the web UI is built. The Host guard still applies; the Docker `HEALTHCHECK` calls `http://127.0.0.1:$PORT/api/health` from inside the container with `node -e fetch(...)`, so the runtime image needs no curl or wget.

codeRefs.note: Version reported by the health check: ARCHWEAVE_VERSION, else package.json

notes.text: Add GET /api/health returning status, version and the model revision. Use it for a HEALTHCHECK in the Dockerfile. Must work without the web UI being built.

elements.name: Inspector
elements.summary: Side panel to read and edit the selected element, relation thread or flow step: fields, notes, code refs, relations, data.

elements.name: Integrity check
elements.summary: Finds graph problems a schema cannot: duplicate ids, unknown references, non-data data refs, containment cycles.
elements.description: Used whenever a model enters from outside the store (startup load, disk reload) and by the change engine after every change set, so no change set can persist a model that would not load. A loaded model with problems is refused: startup exits with the list, a reload is ignored and logged; a change set with problems is a validation error.

elements.name: JournalEntry
elements.summary: One line of the shared activity journal: who changed what, at which revision.

elements.name: state/journal.jsonl
elements.summary: The activity journal, one JournalEntry per line, last 500 kept. Git-ignored.
elements.description: Read at startup to restore the journal and the revision counter; malformed lines are skipped with a log message.

elements.name: Layout
elements.summary: Diagram positions per canvas, kept out of the model.
elements.description: Canvas keys are `structure:<scopeId>` (or `structure:root`) and `data`; each maps element id → `{x, y}`. Written by the browser (auto-placement and dragging); agents must not send it.

elements.name: layout.json
elements.summary: Persisted diagram positions, canvases and ids sorted, coordinates rounded. Committed to Git.

elements.name: MCP endpoint
elements.summary: Exposes the model to coding agents as MCP tools at /mcp and ships the modeling guide as server instructions.
elements.description:
Stateless Streamable HTTP: each POST creates a fresh `McpServer` + transport (JSON responses, no session id); GET is refused with 405. Any request marks the agent present (`Session.touchAgent`) with the `clientInfo.name` from `initialize`.

Tools: `get_guide`, `get_context`, `get_model`, `get_element`, `search`, `find_by_code`, `apply_changes` (actor `agent`, `dryRun` supported), `check_code_links`, `get_changes`, `focus_ui`, `export`.

`get_context` and `apply_changes` return the human's changes since the agent's cursor and then advance it, so the agent sees each human edit once.

elements.name: MCP shell client
elements.summary: Command-line MCP client for agents and scripts without a native MCP connection.
elements.description: `node scripts/mcp-call.mjs instructions | tools | <tool> [json | @file.json]`. Speaks real MCP (Streamable HTTP) via the official SDK; `ARCHWEAVE_URL` selects the server and `ARCHWEAVE_CLIENT` the client name shown as agent presence. JSON results are pretty-printed when stdout is a terminal or `ARCHWEAVE_PRETTY=1`, one line otherwise (`ARCHWEAVE_PRETTY=0` forces one line).

elements.name: Model
elements.summary: The whole architecture: one graph of elements and relations plus flows; perspectives are lenses onto it.
elements.description: Independent of diagram rendering — positions live in Layout so model diffs stay semantic.

elements.name: Model edits
elements.summary: Edit commands shared by canvas, keyboard, inspector and palette: create, connect, reparent, delete, rename.

elements.name: model.json
elements.summary: The persisted model in canonical form: sorted by id, defaults omitted. Committed to Git.
elements.description: Written atomically (temp file + rename) 150 ms after a change. Edits on disk (git checkout/pull, manual) are reloaded; a model with integrity problems is refused.

elements.name: Model schema
elements.summary: Zod schemas and types for the model, change sets, journal, session state, plus id and path helpers.

elements.name: Model store
elements.summary: Single in-memory owner of model, layout, revision, journal and undo; every mutation goes through it.
elements.description: `apply(changeSet, actor)` validates and applies atomically, bumps the revision, records a journal entry (last 500) and an undo step (last 50), then notifies subscribers. A change set whose `expectedRevision` is not the current revision throws `RevisionConflict` and applies nothing; `preview` (dry run) checks it too. Layout-only change sets ignore `expectedRevision`, are neither journaled nor undoable and do not bump the revision. `replace` takes over a model/layout reloaded from disk (clears undo); `undo` restores the previous model but keeps the human's current arrangement.

elements.name: Model views
elements.summary: Read-side projections the MCP tools return: outline, expanded element, search, find-by-code and the data perspective.
elements.description: `ModelView` indexes one model snapshot and builds the agent-facing shapes: compact elements, outlines with lifted relation threads, fully expanded elements/relations, data users and field refs, ranked search results and code-path lookups. `dataCatalog` and `dataFocus` describe the data perspective for `get_context` the way the browser draws it.

elements.name: Modeled repository
elements.summary: The codebase being modeled; read-only source of files for code links, the code drawer and stale-link checks.
elements.description: `ARCHWEAVE_REPO_DIR` (default: current directory; `/repo` in Docker). The server only reads it — confined to its real path and never inside `.git` — and lists files with `git ls-files` when available.

elements.name: Modeling guide
elements.summary: The text that tells agents how to structure, name, link and change the model.
elements.description: Sent as the MCP server `instructions` on initialize and returned by the `get_guide` tool. Its "Link the code" section asks for large units to be linked by their declaration line (`symbol` + `startLine`) so links survive edits; "Keep code links working" explains sealing, repairing moved refs with `check_code_links` (`repair: true`) instead of recomputing lines, and fixing changed refs or re-sending them without digest to accept them.

elements.name: Note
elements.summary: A message pinned to an element: human intent for the agent, or an agent's question for the human.

elements.name: Optimistic apply
elements.summary: Applies a change set locally, mirroring the server's upsert semantics closely enough for instant feedback.
elements.description: The server snapshot that follows is always the truth.

elements.name: Persistence
elements.summary: Keeps the data directory in sync with the store: debounced atomic writes and reloads of outside edits.
elements.description: Subscribes to the store and writes pending documents 150 ms after a change (temp file + rename). Watches the directory with `fs.watch`; on a change to `model.json`/`layout.json` it re-reads, compares with the text it last read or wrote (`known`) to tell its own writes from outside edits, and hands real changes to `Store.replace`. An unsaved local edit wins over a concurrent disk change.

elements.name: Relation
elements.summary: A directed edge: `from` acts on `to`, optionally carrying data structures.
elements.description: Generated ids are `<from>-<kind>-<to>` with `-2`, `-3` appended when taken.

fields.name: label
fields.description: Verb phrase shown on the diagram

fields.name: dataIds
fields.description: Data structures carried; must be kind data

elements.name: Repository access
elements.summary: Read-only, path-confined access to the modeled repository: normalize paths, read files, list and fuzzy-search files.
elements.description:
Rejects paths outside the repository (after resolving symlinks) and anything inside `.git`. Files over 1 MiB are truncated; binary files are reported, not returned. File listing uses `git ls-files --cached --others --exclude-standard`, falling back to a directory walk, cached for 5 s.

`info` returns path, type, mtime and size for the code link checker's cache; `resolveSync`/`infoSync` serve the store's synchronous write path, where refs are sealed.

elements.name: REST & event API
elements.summary: Serves the browser: snapshot, change sets, undo, journal, UI state, code files, stale links and their repair, export and the live event stream.
elements.description:
Routes under `/api`:
- `GET /health` (see Health check)
- `GET /snapshot`, `POST /changes` (actor `human`; 409 when `expectedRevision` is out of date), `POST /undo`, `GET /journal?since=`
- `GET /session`, `PUT /session/ui` (what the human sees)
- `GET /events` — SSE: `snapshot`, `agent`, `focus` events, with a keep-alive comment every 25 s; events are queued per connection so they arrive in order
- `GET /code/file?path=`, `GET /code/files?q=&limit=`, `GET /code/stale`
- `POST /code/repair` (optional body `{scopeId}`): re-anchors moved refs as the human
- `GET /export?format=&scope=&perspectives=&code=`

`broadcastStoreChanges` turns every store change into a `snapshot` event carrying the full snapshot (and the journal entry when there is one). `RevisionConflict` maps to 409, `ChangeError`/`PathError` to 400 with `{error, details}`.

elements.name: Server configuration
elements.summary: Where the repository and data live, the listen address and which extra host names are accepted.

fields.name: hostRepoPath
fields.description: ARCHWEAVE_HOST_REPO_PATH, for open-in-editor links from Docker

fields.name: version
fields.description: ARCHWEAVE_VERSION (the Docker image sets it from its VERSION build arg), else the package.json version; reported by the health check and the MCP server info

elements.name: Server event (SSE)
elements.summary: An event pushed to every connected browser over GET /api/events: snapshot, agent presence or focus request.
elements.description: On connect a browser first receives a `snapshot` and an `agent` event. Every store change (apply, undo, disk reload) is broadcast as a `snapshot` with the full snapshot; `entry` is present when the change was journaled (not for reloads or layout-only changes).

elements.name: Server host
elements.summary: Reads configuration, wires the parts together, guards every request and serves the built UI.
elements.description:
`createArchWeave` builds Repo → Persistence (loads files) → Store → Session → routes and the `/mcp` handler on one Hono app.

Guards, applied to every route:
- **hostGuard** refuses requests whose `Host` or `Origin` names a host other than localhost, `HOST` or `ARCHWEAVE_ALLOWED_HOSTS` (DNS-rebinding and cross-site protection).
- **jsonBodyGuard** requires `Content-Type: application/json` on mutating requests with a body, so a plain form post cannot reach the API without a CORS preflight.

`serveWeb` looks for `dist/web/index.html` on every request (a UI built after startup is picked up) and falls back to `index.html` for client-side routes.

elements.name: Server sync
elements.summary: Everything the browser asks of the server: REST calls, the SSE subscription and reporting what the human sees.
elements.description: `api.ts` is the only module that talks HTTP. `bootstrap()` (called once from `main.tsx`) loads snapshot, session and journal, subscribes to `/api/events`, re-fetches stale links after changes (debounced 600 ms), PUTs the UI state 150 ms after it changes, and mirrors perspective/scope/flow in the URL hash so Back drills out.

elements.name: Session
elements.summary: Live, unpersisted state shared by browser and agent: the human's view, agent presence and the browser event bus.
elements.description: Holds the last `UiState` reported by a browser (and when), the agent's presence (connected for 60 s after its last MCP request), the agent's journal cursor and the set of SSE listeners. `publish` fans an event out to every connected browser. Nothing here survives a restart.

elements.name: Session info
elements.summary: GET /api/session response: the last reported UI state, agent presence and repository name.

elements.name: Shared contract
elements.summary: The data contract and structure projection used by server, web UI and MCP tools alike.
elements.description: `src/shared/model.ts` is the single schema (Zod) for the model, change sets, journal entries and session state; `src/shared/projection.ts` computes what a structure canvas shows. Both sides import the same code, so validation and lifting of relations behave identically in browser and server.

elements.name: Snapshot
elements.summary: The full current state at a revision: model plus layout.
elements.description: Returned by `GET /api/snapshot` and carried by every SSE `snapshot` event; the browser always renders the latest one plus its pending edits.

fields.name: revision
fields.description: Bumped by model changes and disk reloads, not by layout-only changes

elements.name: StaleLink
elements.summary: A code ref that no longer matches the repository, with its owner, the reason and, for moved or changed code, a suggested new range.

fields.name: reason
fields.description: moved and changed only for sealed refs

fields.name: step
fields.description: Flow refs: the 1-based step that holds the ref

fields.name: suggestion
fields.description: moved: always, the new range; changed: where the symbol is now, when unambiguous

elements.name: Structure canvas
elements.summary: Draws one scope's children and outside neighbors as nodes with relation threads; drill in, select, connect, drag.
elements.description: Uses the shared structure projection, so relations between descendants are lifted to the visible nodes and merged into threads. Nodes without a stored position are placed around the stored ones with ELK's layered algorithm and committed as a layout-only change set; positions the human set meanwhile win. Stored positions are never replaced automatically; only Tidy re-lays a scope (`layoutAll`).

elements.name: Structure projection
elements.summary: Computes what a structure canvas shows for a scope: children, outside neighbors and relations lifted to them.
elements.description: Shared so the canvas, `get_model`/`get_context` and the Mermaid export agree on what is visible and how relations merge into threads.

elements.name: UiState
elements.summary: What the human is looking at right now: perspective, scope, flow and selection.
elements.description: Pushed by the browser (`PUT /api/session/ui`, debounced 150 ms), held in memory by the Session and read by the agent through `get_context`.

fields.name: scopeId
fields.description: Structure perspective: element whose inside is shown

elements.name: Web UI
elements.summary: Single-page app where the developer views and edits the model in three perspectives: structure, data and flows.
elements.description: Built by Vite into `dist/web` and served by the server. Holds a local copy of the model (server snapshot + optimistic pending changes) in a Zustand store, kept live through the `/api/events` SSE stream. Reports the human's view and selection back to the server so the agent can read it.
elements.technology: React 19, Zustand 5, React Flow 12, ELK, Vite

relations.label: downloads Markdown, Mermaid or JSON export

flows.name: Agent applies a change; the browser updates
flows.summary: An apply_changes call is validated atomically, journaled, broadcast to every browser as a snapshot and saved to disk.

steps.label: apply to a draft copy, all or nothing
steps.description: Removals, upserts, list helpers, referential checks. Any error throws one ChangeError naming every bad entry; nothing is applied.

steps.label: new model and ids, or ChangeError
steps.description: The store bumps the revision, records a journal entry and an undo step, then emits the change synchronously.

steps.label: notify subscriber; schedule a save
steps.description: Debounced 150 ms; several quick changes become one write.

steps.label: ChangeResult (+ human changes since you last looked)
receiveSnapshot; mark touched ids fresh, toast with Show
steps.description: Pending local edits the server has caught up with are dropped; the rest are re-applied on top of the new snapshot.

steps.label: re-render; place new nodes with ELK and commit positions
steps.description: New elements have no position; useAutoPlace lays them out and saves them as a layout-only change set (not journaled).

flows.name: Agent points at something
flows.summary: focus_ui sends a focus event to every browser, which navigates to and highlights the elements with the agent's message.

steps.label: delivered: browsers > 0, or a hint to open the UI

flows.name: Agent repairs code links after editing code
flows.summary: After a code change the agent sees what is linked to the touched files, lets the server re-anchor moved refs in one step, and fixes the edited ones itself.

steps.label: find_by_code(touched paths)
steps.description: Elements, relations and flow steps linked there, each ref with its check.

steps.label: inspect refs
steps.description: Sealed refs are checked by their text: ok, moved (with suggestion) or changed.

steps.label: inspect refs in scope
steps.description: Checks once more if the model or a file changed before the repair could be applied.

steps.label: apply(repair change set)
steps.description: Moved refs get their suggested range and keep their digest; sent with expectedRevision. One journal entry.

steps.label: verify digest at the new range
steps.description: Each relocated ref claims its sealed text now sits at the new range; seal(ref) checks it, and the change set is rejected when it does not match.

steps.label: apply_changes: fix or accept changed refs
steps.description: A wrong ref is replaced (removeCodeRefs + addCodeRefs); a ref that is still right is re-sent without its digest in addCodeRefs, which seals it to its new text.

flows.name: Model files change on disk
flows.summary: After a git checkout or manual edit, the server reloads model.json/layout.json, validates them and pushes the new snapshot to browsers.

steps.label: fs.watch event; reload scheduled after 100 ms
re-read; skip own writes and documents with unsaved edits
steps.description: Compares the file text with what this process last read or wrote. A pending local edit wins and later overwrites the file.

steps.label: schema + integrity; invalid → ignored and logged
steps.description: Nothing changes when the document is invalid; the server keeps the model it has.

steps.label: emit cause 'reload': revision bumped, undo cleared, no journal entry
steps.description: Persistence ignores reload changes, so the file is not written back.

steps.label: receiveSnapshot; drop view references that vanished

flows.name: Export documentation
flows.summary: The developer downloads a Markdown architecture document (or Mermaid/JSON) rendered by the server from the current snapshot.

steps.label: opens Export; picks format, scope, perspectives, code refs
steps.description: PNG/SVG image export is handled in the browser instead: the active canvas is captured with html-to-image.

steps.label: project each scope for its Mermaid flowchart

flows.name: Human edits in the browser
flows.summary: An inspector edit shows at once as a pending change, is applied by the server as the human, and is reconciled when the snapshot arrives.

steps.label: apply locally as pending; shown immediately
Store.apply(changes, 'human')
steps.description: Same path as an agent change: journaled, broadcast, saved.

steps.label: ChangeResult, or error body
steps.description: On success the pending entry is marked acknowledged at that revision; on error it is dropped and an error toast shows.

flows.name: Human selects something; the agent reads it
flows.summary: The browser reports the view and selection; get_context returns them expanded, with open notes and the human's recent edits.

steps.label: store subscription sees the view changed

codeRefs.note: reports the view when it changes and when the event stream reconnects

steps.label: setUi: validate and store with timestamp
read UI state, report time, agent cursor, browser count
snapshot and human journal entries since the cursor
steps.description: The cursor then advances, so each human change is reported once.

steps.label: selection in full, scope, visible elements, open notes, human changes
